Hi Anna / EuroSI team —

Thanks again for the intro call last week. Per our conversation, we'd like to scope a concise mutual action plan to get Redwood listed with your SI network in the EU and to confirm a reseller pathway in APAC. Two lead items we need to align on before an NDA/SOW draft:

1) Data residency and logging: what are the expectations for log retention locations (EU-only for EU customers?), and are you comfortable with our dedicated/Private deployment options for EU-regulated customers?
2) Marketplace and procurement requirements in APAC: any local partner certification or legal language (e.g., reseller margins, invoice routing) we should bake into the SOW?

Attached a lightweight SOW template and a short checklist that usually helps speed legal review. Can you review and highlight any must-haves on your side?

Proposed next steps:
- EuroSI to flag any data residency redlines by Fri, Feb 20
- Redwood (Vivek/Karthik) to propose reseller commercial terms by Mon, Feb 23
- Schedule technical kickoff (30 min) the week of Feb 23 to cover connectors and on-prem installers for APAC pilots

Appreciate any context (GCP/Azure region constraints, KMS/HSM preferences) so our infra team can prepare.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Regional partnership kickoff — EU SIs & APAC resellers (data residency items)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear plan. Quick answers from EuroSI side:

- EU data residency: for our enterprise customers in EU regulated sectors (finance, health), logs and any customer-controlled data must be stored in EU regions only. We can accept a dedicated Private deployment (VPC) when customers require it. For hosted API customers we typically require EU-hosted tenancy and KMS keys within the EU.
- APAC reseller path: in JP/AU we need a local reseller agreement with invoice-to options and a minimal local certification (security questionnaire + supplier onboarding). We rarely require on-prem for APAC pilots, but having a lightweight on-prem installer for pilot sites is a plus.

Attached an internal checklist and our standard onboarding matrix — highlights: proof of SOC2 or equivalent, data processing addendum (DPA) with EU SCCs, and a point on data deletion SLA.

We reviewed the SOW template: overall fine but please add the following clauses:
- explicit data residency clause for EU customers
- option for customer-driven Private deployment (fees TBD)
- reseller invoicing flow for APAC

I propose a 30-minute technical sync Fri (Feb 20) 09:00 CET / 17:00 JST to land technical expectations. Does that work?

Best,
Anna Keller
Head of Strategic Partnerships | EuroSI
anna.keller@euroSI.com
Attachment: EU_Data_Residency_QA.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks Marissa — quick infra notes:

- EU residency: we already support EU-hosted tenancy for hosted API; logs can be routed to EU-owned buckets and KMS keys in the EU. For Private deployments we can enforce local storage and KMS integration, but there is a one-time engineering validation fee and a small monthly operating premium.
- HSM/KMS: we integrate with GCP CMEK, Azure KeyVault and customer-managed AWS KMS. For regulated EU customers, recommend CMEK in EU regions or bring-your-own-key to avoid cross-border exports.
- On-prem installer: infra can provide a lightweight OVA/containerized installer for APAC pilots; needs a short acceptance test (we can bundle into the SOW).

I'll draft a short infra appendix for the SOW that enumerates options and cost bands; will share by EOD Mon (Feb 23 PST).
